gen-dafont-stentiga-gf-liter: Liter reads as a plain sans with no stroke contrast at all, and its lowercase stands up with real presence. And Stentiga's spread-out tracking and wide-open letter gaps give the heading a refined, luxurious feel above it.
gen-dafont-stentiga-gf-mada: Stentiga draws every stroke at a single constant width, spaced out and luxurious. Mada underneath has curves that refuse to close and a towering midzone, so the pair's strongest quality is how a hairline-steady display face meets a body with real stroke variation.
gen-dafont-stentiga-gf-martel-sans: Stentiga spreads its refined display letters out, with curves and straights drawn at one line width. Martel Sans prefers generous openings and a high mean line.
gen-dafont-stentiga-gf-maven-pro: Maven Pro opens things up with a welcoming gap in its c and a gentle, monotone line, giving the sans a high-waisted lowercase. Maven Pro and Stentiga together are modern and refined, the spread-out luxury of one lending polish to the other.
gen-dafont-stentiga-gf-michroma: Stentiga's stroke looks drawn with a ballpoint pen, steady and spread out. It shows its best in refined display lettering, while Michroma does its best work giving each letter a wide berth, with curves that leave daylight and stubby ascender tips.
gen-dafont-stentiga-gf-miriam-libre: Miriam Libre reads approachably, with generous openings in its s and the weight of a drawn wire, and its lowercase has the stature of cast iron capitals. Stentiga, by contrast, does its best work as refined, luxurious display lettering with open tracking and wide letter gaps.
gen-dafont-stentiga-gf-mochiy-pop-p-one: Stentiga spreads its refined, luxurious letters out with wide-open gaps. Mochiy Pop P One would read as a sizable, friendly plain sans over a long passage, with generous blank space between letters and no brush-like swell to slow the eye.
gen-dafont-stentiga-gf-montserrat-underl: Montserrat Underline reads open and professional, with breathing counters, round bowls of unwavering wall thickness and an oversized lowercase. But Stentiga does the refined, luxurious part, using spread-out tracking for display, where the sans-serif body simply carries the text.
gen-dafont-stentiga-gf-mozilla-headline: Mozilla Headline reads approachably, with big-bodied lowercase and a splayed terminal on its c. Yet Stentiga does the refined display work, its thickness holding steady around every curve, while the body carries the text with more stroke variation.
gen-dafont-stentiga-gf-mozilla-text: Stentiga draws a plain stripe of constant ink, spread out and luxurious. Mozilla Text would carry a longer passage with bold-looking lowercase from its big bodies, and terminals that flare outward to keep the lines moving.
